RFC8666-10-1.note: RA-OSPF2 strict re-audit 2026-09-27 (independent of DF-OSPF-E). RFC 8666 Section 10 (rfc8666.txt, s10): 'For any new TLVs/sub-TLVs defined in this document, if the length is invalid, the LSA in which it is advertised is considered malformed and MUST be ignored.' Kept weak; DF-OSPF-E's gaps confirmed. Proven through the IPv6 Prefix-SID reader (srRemotePrefixSIDsV6, len(sids) != 0 goes red): Prefix-SID one octet too long (TestRFC8666LengthInvalidSubTLVIgnoresExtendedLSA), too short, length-and-flags, Extended Prefix Range carrying a length-and-flags-invalid Prefix-SID (TestRFC8666LengthBeforeFlagsIgnoresLSA), with positive polarity for well-formed and flag-only cases. Unproven: the Adj-SID and LAN Adj-SID clauses are asserted only on the gate srV3ExtendedLengthInvalid, never on a reader that ignores the LSA; LAN Adj-SID too short has no case; the SID/Label sub-TLV (s3.1) has no LSA-level case.

RFC8666-11-1.note: malformed values are rejected with an error (not only no panic) by every v3 SR decoder and by v6PrefixSIDFromPrefixTLV; well-formed range TLVs still decode

RFC8666-5-1.note: single-polarity positive: v6EInterAreaPrefixBody (the only range producer) decodes to Range Size 1 for a /128; 1 never exceeds what any Prefix Length satisfies

RFC8666-5-2.note: positive asserts the encoded Flags octet is zero; the other tag sets Flags=0xFF and asserts header, address and Prefix-SID decode unchanged

RFC8666-5-7.note: 0xFFFFFF in Reserved decodes identically to zero (and encoder sends zero); negative bounds the ignore by showing the adjacent AF octet is honoured

RFC8666-6-1.note: NP set through the real OSPFv3 carriage and installer: push 16009, swap 18009->16009, no pop entry; negative shows NP clear does pop

RFC8666-6-11.note: NP clear programs a PHP pop of 18009 and no push or swap; negative: NP set programs no pop

RFC8666-6-12.note: NP set, E clear keeps the SRGB label on the stack (push 16009, swap to 16009); negative: NP clear pops

RFC8666-6-13.note: NP+E set replaces the SID with Explicit NULL 2 at ingress and in the swap; negative: NP set, E clear does not

RFC8666-6-14.note: M=1,NP=0,E=1 keeps 16009 with no pop and no Explicit NULL (both flags ignored); same input without M pops

RFC8666-6-2.note: NP+E set imposes ExplicitNullV6 (2) at ingress and in the transit swap; E clear imposes the SRGB label. IPv4 clause (label 0) does not arise: OSPFv3 reception rejects a non-IPv6 AF

RFC8666-6-3.note: all defined flags set encode as 0x7C with bits 0/6/7 clear; reserved bits 0x83 set on receive decode identically

RFC8666-6-4.note: Reserved=0xFFFF decodes identically; negative bounds the ignore to Reserved by showing the Algorithm octet is honoured

RFC8666-6-5.note: algorithm 0 not in the originator's SR-Algorithm list installs no mpls-fib entry; advertised algorithm installs push 16009

RFC8666-6-6.note: V=1/L=0 and V=0/L=1 are rejected by DecodePrefixSIDValueV6, whose error drops the TLV in v6PrefixSIDFromTLV; valid V/L pairs decode

RFC8666-6-7.note: RA-OSPF2 strict re-audit 2026-09-27 (independent of DF-OSPF-E). RFC 8666 Section 6 (rfc8666.txt:380-381): 'If an OSPFv3 router advertises multiple Prefix-SIDs for the same prefix, topology, and algorithm, all of them MUST be ignored.' Proven clauses: one router's repeated Prefix-SID, equal (TestRFC8666OneRouterMultiplePrefixSIDsAllIgnored positive, two sub-TLVs and two LSAs) or differing (TestRFC8666PrefixSIDsKeyedByAlgorithm positive), each asserting rs.Duplicate; scope limits prefix, algorithm, router and area kept in the negative cases. Topology: the RFC 8666 Prefix-SID sub-TLV carries Flags, Algorithm, Reserved and SID only (s6 figure), so there is no second topology value to test. Weak because no tagged unit proves the consequence 'ignored': every assertion stops at the Duplicate marker. Removing `|| rs.Duplicate` from the installer (sr_install.go:80) leaves every RFC8666-6-7 unit green (only the RFC8665-tagged TestRFC8665DuplicatePrefixSIDsAllIgnored goes red), and removing it from srTILFAResolver.PrefixSIDLabel (sr_tilfa.go:40) leaves them green too (work/agents/RA-OSPF2/mutation.log). The cross-router tests TestRFC8666DuplicatePrefixSIDsDetectedAndIgnored and TestOSPFv3ReceptionSameSIDNotDuplicate no longer carry this tag, correctly: they prove Ze policy.

RFC8666-6-8.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 (continuation 5). Positive: new TestRFC8666NextHopAdvertisedFlagsShapeOutgoingLabel, next hop = SID advertiser, four flag settings each give the Section 6 outcome: NP clear -> no push and PHP pop of 18009; NP -> push 16009; NP+E -> push IPv6 Explicit NULL; M+E with NP clear -> push 16009 (M makes NP and E ignored, distinguishable from the NP-clear pop). Negative: TestRFC8666TransitHopIgnoresOriginatorPHPFlags, a non-advertising next hop does not apply the originator's NP=0; judge overlay applying the flags unconditionally in forwarding (sr_install.go) reds it. Revert record on forwarding observed red for the positive. TestRFC8666OutgoingLabelUsesNextHopRouter stays tagged as supplementary (next hop's SRGB).

RFC8666-6-9.note: v6InterAreaPrefixSIDRule sets NP and clears E for a propagated prefix and keeps flags when directly attached; TestOSPFv3OriginateInterAreaPropagation asserts NP set/E clear on the real propagated LSA

RFC8666-7.1-1.note: all defined Adj-SID flags encode 0xF8 with bits 5-7 clear; 0x07 set on receive decodes identically

RFC8666-7.1-2.note: Reserved=0xFFFF decodes identically and encoder sends zero; negative bounds the ignore by showing Weight is honoured

RFC8666-7.2-1.note: LAN Adj-SID Reserved=0xFFFF decodes identically and encoder sends zero; negative shows Neighbor ID is honoured

RFC8666-8.2-1.note: intra-area Prefix-SID learned in area 1 is re-originated by v6OriginateInterAreaSR into the backbone E-Inter-Area-Prefix-LSA and not back into area 1
